findings.title: Embedded-post author links use the opposite lightness mapping
findings.body: The original light-theme color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but this now uses `$primary` at 70% and `$secondary` at 30%. This changes the established light-theme appearance and darkens the dark-theme counterpart instead of using the corresponding `$secondary` 70% value. Use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))` so embedded reply author links retain their intended contrast in both themes.

findings.title: Desktop group-member names lost their intended stronger color
findings.body: `.group-member-info .name` previously used `$primary` at 30%, while the title used 50%. The new expression changes the name to 50% in the light theme and 50% in the dark theme, making it identical to the title and failing to provide the expected dark-theme counterpart. Preserve the original 30% primary branch and use `$secondary` at 70% for dark themes.

findings.title: Mobile custom-message length text has the light/dark lightness values reversed
findings.body: This rule originally used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, but the new expression uses `$primary` at 30% and `$secondary` at 70%. That changes the light-theme text color and is inconsistent with the equivalent desktop modal rule. It should retain the 70% primary branch and use `$secondary` at 30% for the dark-theme branch.

findings.title: Mobile topic-map heading no longer preserves its heading contrast
findings.body: The topic-map `h3` originally used `$primary` at 20%, but the new expression changes both branches to 50%. This makes the h3 the same tone as the following h4 rule and removes the established visual hierarchy in light themes, while also failing to use the corresponding dark-theme value. The paired expression should be `$primary` at 20% and `$secondary` at 80%.

findings.title: Mobile group-member names lost their intended stronger color
findings.body: `.group-member-info .name` previously used `$primary` at 30%, distinct from the 50% title color. The replacement uses 50% for both primary and secondary, changing the light-theme color and collapsing that distinction. Use the preserved 30% primary value with `$secondary` at 70% for the dark-theme counterpart.
